tools (ai/tool/*) and agents, which are not functions, and tasks, are not covered by any rule
whether endpoint_path snake_case applies to path parameters such as {customer_id} is unknown from the catalogue
flagging rather than blocking: honoured by enforcement=advisory, not a check

assumptions: Client prefix is acme_ (taken from existing workspace function names acme_calculate_tax, acme_get_tracking, acme_notify_sms, acme_send_invoice_email, acme_sync_shipping_rates)
Plural means ends in s, the proxy the suffix rule can express
Advisory and active, severity low (matches the other convention templates)
A single policy with three rules, since the customer asked for one policy covering the three naming parts
workspace_names_used: tables: audit_log, invoice_item, payment_method, user_address (non-plural, predicted to be flagged); orgs, sessions, customers, orders and others pass
endpoints: getCustomerProfile (camelCase query name), bank-accounts/link (path uses kebab-case), customers/{customer_id}, payments/{payment_id}

functions: acme_calculate_tax, acme_get_tracking, acme_notify_sms, acme_send_invoice_email, acme_sync_shipping_rates (prefixed); calculateLateFee, calculate_late_fee, check_admin_role, delete_user_account, record_audit_event, request_human_approval, summarize_ticket (not prefixed)
existing policies: none (xano policy list printed 'No policies found.')
confusions: The skill's naming rules say a suffix is literal text and an irregular plural needs allowed_names; it does not say whether a plural suffix check reads the whole name or the last word. I assumed the whole name.

CONV-012 is kebab-case and the customer asked for snake_case; the guidance says to change its case_style rather than add a second policy, but this customer has no CONV-012 in place, so it was unclear whether to mention the template's kebab-case at all.

Template key guidance: 'a template prefix such as AUTH- or DATA- with a number no template has' is unclear for a custom key; I used CLIENT-NAMING, which avoids the prefix problem but leaves no guidance on what a custom naming key should look like.
Whether endpoint_path case checks apply to path parameters in braces (customers/{customer_id}) is not stated anywhere in the catalogue or templates.

The brief said use the workspace's real names; the workspace pull gives file names like customer_id_PATCH.xs that differ from the endpoint paths inside them. I used the paths from the file body, which took extra reading.
wished_for: A template or recipe for naming conventions that takes a client prefix as a fill (the customer's stated use case: many clients, same shape, different prefix)
A 'plural' option for object.naming, or a note that the suffix check is not a real plural check
A statement on whether endpoint_path checks cover path params
A recipe for advisory-only naming policies, since the customer asked to flag rather than block
parse_errors_seen: Policy parse failed: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'out/CLIENT-NAMING.xs' (path was relative to the wrong directory; not a policy error)
why_confidence: The policy parses and the three checks cover the three parts of the ask. Confidence is medium because the client prefix is assumed, the plural check is only a trailing-s proxy, and no evaluation was run (evaluate is forbidden for this task), so the predicted findings are not verified.
